title: Missouri Woman Charged After Shot Fired in Neighbours' Fence Dispute
excerpt: Paula Kohensky, 60, faces first-degree assault and armed criminal action charges in St. Charles County. The neighbour was unhurt, and the two sides give conflicting accounts.
body:
• Paula Kohensky, 60, of St. Charles County, Missouri, is charged with first-degree assault and armed criminal action after a shot was fired toward a neighbour repairing a fence, according to court records cited by Law&Crime.
  • The neighbour was not injured. He told police he heard yelling, a countdown of "3, 2, 1," then a gunshot; Kohensky told police the gun discharged accidentally.
  • Police said home security video showed Kohensky pointing a gun toward the fence, and investigators found a casing and a suspected bullet hole in a tarp.
  • Court records set bond at $500,000. Reports differ on custody status, and a preliminary hearing is scheduled for December 2.

A months-long property-line dispute in St. Charles County, Missouri, has become a felony case. Paula Kohensky, 60, is charged with first-degree assault and armed criminal action after police said she fired a handgun toward a neighbour who was repairing a fence on Sunday night, according to court records reviewed by Law&Crime and reported by The Times of India.

Two Accounts of One Gunshot

The neighbour told investigators he had misaligned a metal T-post and was using an electric side grinder to cut it at ground level when he heard yelling, then a voice counting "3, 2, 1," followed by a gunshot, according to the probable cause statement summarised by Law&Crime reporting. He picked up the post and went inside, and his wife called police. He was not injured.

Kohensky gave a different account. She told police she had gone into her backyard with a handgun, heard a loud metallic sound and saw sparks under a tarp, shouted "Get away from my fence" at what she believed was her neighbour's shadow, and said the firearm discharged accidentally. She also told police she had a history of harassment and stalking concerns involving the neighbours, according to the reports.

What Investigators Say the Video Shows

Police said security video from the neighbour's home showed Kohensky and her husband in the backyard before the shooting, with the handgun dipping in a movement investigators described as consistent with recoil anticipation. Investigators reported finding a spent casing near where she stood and a suspected bullet hole in the tarp covering the fence. Her husband, who has not been charged, was reported to have taken the gun inside, where police later found it in the living room.

Charges and Next Steps

Kohensky faces one count of first-degree assault or attempted assault and one count of armed criminal action. Court records cited in the reports set a $500,000 cash-only bond; Law&Crime reported she was released after posting $50,000, while other reports described her as held on the $500,000 bond. A preliminary hearing is scheduled for December 2. The charges are allegations, and Kohensky is presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.
